meta.description: Curated Thok Nath ↔ English sentence pairs for few-shot prompting in Naath AI
sources: Nuer Bible (RUAC KUƆTH IN RƐL RƆ) — Bible Society in South Sudan
key_grammar_reminders: Negation prefix /: always attached directly to the word — /Cu, /Ciɛ, /Kän (never / Cu)
Past tense: Cu (3rd person), Cä (I did), Ci̱ (was). Negative past: /Kän
Future tense: bɛ (he/she/they), bä (I), ba (we). Pronoun comes BEFORE marker: jɛn bɛ wä
Copula ɛ = 'to be' (present positive). /Ciɛɛ = am/is not, /Ci̱kɛ = are not
Kinship terms are inherently possessive: maar=my mother, gua̱a̱r=my father, dämaar=my brother, nyimaar=my sister
Question marker: ɔ? at end for yes/no. Ɛŋa? = who, Ɛŋu? = what, Rɛy ŋa? = where/when
Conjunction kä = and/then/but. ɣöö = that/because/so that. mi = who/which/when/that
Cardinal directions: Caam = North, Cueec = South, Nhiam = East, Jɔk = West

examples.nuer: “Kɛ ɣöö nhɔk Kuoth nɛy diaal ɛlɔ̱ŋ, cuɛ Gatdɛ kɛl ni kärɔa muɔc, kɛ ɣöö ram mi wä jɛ ŋäth, /cɛ bi li̱w, bɛ tekɛ tëk mi thil pek.
